title: Blaschka auction provenance cross-links and market-adjacent leads
purpose: Supplement the canonical auction lot table with cross-source identity hypotheses, prior institutional labels, dealer-market leads, and bounded negative-search results that should not be flattened into auction facts without an explicit evidential bridge.

relationship_to_canonical.rule: This file records evidence that qualifies or extends canonical auction records without silently upgrading inferred buyer identities, dealer transactions, institutional labels, or conflicting dates into settled provenance.

evidence: Invaluable indexes Grisebach lot 483 on 26 November 2015 for a Blaschka Serpulidae model labelled Serpula contortuplicata, L. No. 343, with dimensions approximately 6 cm high by 9.5 cm diameter and estimate EUR 3,000-5,000.
Catalogue metadata identifies the sale as Grisebach sale 249, ORANGERIE. Selected Objects, Berlin, 26 November 2015, lots 400-485.

In a first-person Corning Museum of Glass guest post, George Loudon states that after publishing his 2015 book he had recently found a Blaschka Serpulidae worm at auction in Berlin; the illustrated object is identified as Serpula contortuplicata and measured 6 x 9 cm diameter, with a 2015 Berlin photograph credit.
Taxon, object type, city, time, dimensions and 2015 documentation align very closely, but Loudon's account does not name Grisebach, sale 249, lot 483 or L. No. 343.
crosslinks.safe_public_claim: George Loudon's 2016 first-person account appears to describe the same Serpula contortuplicata model catalogued as Grisebach sale 249, lot 483 in Berlin on 26 November 2015, but the buyer identity remains an inference until a buyer record, invoice, catalogue annotation, or explicit collection crosswalk is recovered.
open_fields: explicit buyer record or invoice linking lot 483 to George Loudon

crosslinks.prior_institutional_label: Zoolog. Institut Universität, Berlin / handwritten botanical designation
crosslinks.institutional_interpretation: The wording is consistent with a Berlin university zoological-institute teaching-collection label. It establishes a prior Berlin institutional association at label level, not an original-purchase, legal-title, deaccession, or current-institution identity by itself.

date_conflict.Berlin_institutional_collection_context: Museum für Naturkunde Berlin identifies a historical Blaschka collection in its object collection OS001; the object-level dating relationship remains unresolved until inventory crosswalk.
date_conflict.guard: Do not assume that the label places the object in the surviving MfN/HU corpus without an inventory crosswalk.

crosslinks.condition_from_primary_page: Glass case with light signs of use and light soiling; top pane and right-side pane each with a small corner crack; otherwise overall good condition.
crosslinks.institutional_interpretation: Like lot 26, lot 27 carries an explicit Berlin zoological-institute university label. This is prior institutional provenance evidence, but no Berlin inventory number, deaccession record, or HU/MfN object-level crosswalk is yet public.

date_conflict.Berlin_institutional_collection_context: Museum für Naturkunde Berlin identifies a historical Blaschka collection in OS001 and exposes an inventory target OS001-02.

crosslinks.next_step: Search the MfN OS001-02 Blaschka inventory list and HU zoological teaching-collection records for matching sea-anemone/polyp morphology, old labels, catalogue numbers, dimensions or movement/deaccession notes.

crosslinks.guard: Retain as secondary result reporting until a Christie's results record or another primary result source is recovered.

market_adjacent_leads.former_holder_status: first-person collector testimony reports an English school; a separate collector interview calls it a public school

reported_object_batch_breakdown.objects: ten models of slugs and snails

market_adjacent_leads.reported_context: Loudon states that the London-based dealer's entire Blaschka stock came from an English school that closed its natural-history department for financial reasons. A separate interview characterises the source as a public school quietly disposing of the models.

book_count_crosslink.source_statement: Loudon says his 2015 book covered 200 works including 15 Blaschkas.
book_count_crosslink.inference: The dealer/school batch totals exactly 15, making it highly plausible that the 15 Blaschkas in the 2015 book are the school-derived dealer group.
book_count_crosslink.guard: Do not treat the arithmetic match as proof that every Blaschka in the 2015 book came from that school unless the book captions, dealer records or object labels close the crosswalk.

post_book_berlin_acquisition.reported_timing: described in 2016 as recently found at auction in Berlin after the 2015 book statement
post_book_berlin_acquisition.possible_count_implication: The sequence could raise Loudon's Blaschka holding from the book's 15 to at least 16, but this remains an inference rather than a canonical current-holding count.

later_public_presence.event: The University Museum, University of Tokyo / Intermediatheque exhibition displayed 14 Blaschka glass specimens among 50 selected Loudon collection items.
later_public_presence.interpretation: An exhibition selection is not a full collection inventory and cannot be used to reduce or fix Loudon's holding count at 14.

market_adjacent_leads.why_not_auction_record: The school-derived group was acquired through a dealer, not through a documented public auction. It is therefore retained as a provenance-gap lead but excluded from auction lot totals.
open_fields: object-level crosswalk between the 15 school/dealer models and the 15 Blaschkas in Object Lessons
model catalogue numbers and later/current custody

institutional_context_only.statement: UCL states that when the Science Museum deaccessioned its glass-model collection between 1925 and 1927, models were transferred to UCL and six other institutions. Museum Wales independently records a 1927 transfer of 62 models from the Science Museum to Cardiff.
institutional_context_only.guard: Do not infer that the three 2019 Christie's lots were transferred to UCL, Cardiff or any of the other institutions without matching Science Museum transfer/disposal records or recipient accession numbers.

bounded_negative_search.result: No additional vetted physical Blaschka auction lot was promoted in this continuation pass.
areas_rechecked: English, German, French and Italian keyword variants
exact label phrases including Blaschka's Modelle and L. No.

bounded_negative_search.important_negative_guard: Search-engine and public-index failure is not catalogue exhaustion. Older PDF, print-only, poorly OCRed, subscriber-only and unindexed sale catalogues remain outside the closure claim.
